identity.notes: `mac` is the six bytes of register 0x84, read after connecting, printed most-significant octet first (9c:9a:c0:dd:ee:ff as a placeholder). The on-air address rotates and must be treated as a connection locator only. Every brick advertises the same name; the owner's chosen name is register 0x80.

manufacturer_data.description: LEGO company id 0x0397 (little-endian 97 03 on the air). Payload bytes after it are device-specific and undocumented.

methods.notes: The service UUID 0000fef6-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb is advertised too, but it is shared by every Cordio WDX product, so it is left out of this matcher on purpose (a ble_scan matcher ORs name and service). Confirm with a connectable advertisement and, after connecting, the Device Information manufacturer string "LEGO".

host_compatibility.basis: node-smartplay's captures are Android HCI snoop logs of the vendor app connecting to and driving a docked brick.

manufacturer_data.description: LEGO System A/S in the Bluetooth SIG company list. The payload after the company id was 00 60 00 00 00 00 in upstream's capture; its meaning is not known, so nothing matches on it.

identification.notes: Match all three together. 0xFEF6 is a SIG member UUID assigned to Wicentric (the stack's original author), so every product built on the Cordio WDX profile advertises it. Company 0x0397 is on every LEGO BLE product, the Powered Up hubs included. The name "Smart Brick" is the brick's. The advertised address is an LE random address that rotates often, so there is no usable MAC prefix on the air: the brick's real MAC, under LEGO's OUI 9c:9a:c0, is only readable from register 0x84 after connecting. A "Smart Brick" advertisement that is not connectable (ADV_NONCONN_IND) is a brick in multi-brick play, not one a client can use.

device.name: LEGO Smart Play Smart Brick
device.notes:
The SMART Brick is the 2x4 electronic brick at the centre of LEGO's SMART Play system (2026): speaker and sound synthesiser, LED array, accelerometer, colour and light sensing, a microphone for sound pressure, and coils that charge it wirelessly, read SMART Tags and SMART Minifigures, and sense nearby bricks. It plays on its own with no phone. The LEGO SMART Assist app is for grown-ups: it shows battery level, registers the brick to a LEGO account and installs firmware updates.
This spec covers one mode only: the brick talking to a phone while it sits on its SMART Charger. It is connectable only if it STARTED UP on the charger. Upstream's firmware analysis says the brick checks for the dock once, at boot, and only then turns on connectable advertising; nothing later (motion, play, a timer, being placed on the charger while running) turns it on. A brick that started off the charger either does not advertise at all or, during multi-brick play, advertises "Smart Brick" without accepting connections.
Everything runs over the WDX service (0xFEF6) of the Arm Cordio BLE stack, which the brick's EM Microelectronic EM9305 SoC runs. One characteristic, the Control Point 005f0002-2ff2-4ed5-b045-4c7463617865, carries a register protocol: read is 01 RR, write is 02 RR VV..., and the brick answers 03 RR VV... by notification. Registers 0x01-0x25 are the stock Cordio WDX device configuration set; 0x80-0x96 are LEGO's. The unauthenticated surface is real and useful: model, firmware version, battery, name (read and write), volume (read and write), MAC, upgrade state and a keepalive.
Privileged operations (unlock, telemetry consent, factory reset, the start of a firmware upgrade, diagnostics, ownership proof) need an ECDSA P-256 signature over a per-connection nonce. The private key is held by LEGO's servers, not by the app or the brick; the app asks LEGO's backend to sign. No replacement client can do these offline, and this spec gives no way round that: it documents the layout so an implementer recognises the exchange and knows what it cannot do.
Out of scope: brick-to-brick play (Bluetooth 5.4 PAwR on a separate address, with its own internal registers 0x1B, 0x1C and reuses of 0x25 and 0x26), the WDX file-transfer channels (firmware images, telemetry, fault log), LEGO Powered Up / BOOST / SPIKE hubs (LWP3, a different protocol) and MINDSTORMS NXT/EV3 (Bluetooth Classic). SMART Tag events are not on the BLE surface at all: upstream's firmware analysis found no register or notification that reports a tag.

enter_pairing_mode.indicator: None documented on the brick. The charger's LED shows the battery state (red, yellow or green), not connectability. A scan shows a connectable "Smart Brick" advertisement with service 0xFEF6.
enter_pairing_mode.notes: "Pairing mode" here means connectable mode: the brick accepts a connection only if it booted on the dock. Upstream reads the firmware as checking the dock type once at boot (two dock types qualify) and never again, and restarting advertising after every disconnect without re-checking, so a brick that started docked probably stays connectable when lifted off. That last point is upstream's inference, not an observation.

procedures.basis: node-smartplay research/notes/PROTOCOL.md, 'When Is The Brick Connectable?' (firmware analysis plus radio captures); LEGO's getting-started page for shake-to-wake and the charger.
procedures.name: Start the brick on the SMART Charger

steps.action: With the brick asleep, set it on a SMART Charger and wake it there. LEGO's guide says a SMART Brick wakes when shaken; whether being set on the charger alone starts it is not documented.
Scan for a connectable "Smart Brick" advertisement.

exclusivity.notes: Neither upstream source says how many centrals the brick accepts at once.
exclusivity.recovery: Close the SMART Assist app (or disconnect the other client) before connecting. If a phone has bonded with the brick and misbehaves, forget the brick in that phone's Bluetooth settings.

pairing.notes: Link layer: nothing is required. node-smartplay connects and drives the whole unauthenticated surface with no pairing. Reading register 0x86 (the signed-command nonce) makes the brick request link-layer pairing; the association model (Just Works or otherwise) and whether the vendor app keeps the bond are not documented, hence `bonding: optional`. The real authorisation is application-layer: the ECDSA P-256 signed command in protocol_details.signed_command, which only LEGO's backend can produce.

unpair.notes: The stock WDX register set has a delete-bonds register (0x07, write), but neither upstream source says LEGO's firmware implements it or that the app uses it. Forgetting the brick in the phone's Bluetooth settings drops the phone's half of a bond.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi. A local client needs no credential for the unauthenticated surface and cannot obtain one for the signed surface: each signature covers one per-connection nonce and is made by LEGO's backend for the signed-in owner.
stored_on_device: The ECDSA P-256 public key the firmware checks signed commands against (fixed in firmware; public, not a secret).
Registration/ownership and consent state set by signed commands (contents not documented).
Link-layer bond data if a central has paired (upstream's flash-layout notes list a parameter area holding it).

factory_reset.description: Upstream's register map and signed-command table show the reset exists and is gated by a signature only LEGO's backend can produce, so the vendor app is the only route. No button or charger gesture is known to reset the brick; the brick has no buttons.
factory_reset.effect: Not established. The firmware has a factory-reset register (0x95) that acts only after a server-signed command; what it clears (registration, name, volume, consent, bonds) is not documented. Firmware is not expected to change.

procedures.basis: node-smartplay research/notes/PROTOCOL.md register map (factory reset, auth required) and its signed-command table (type 3, factory reset); where the option sits in the app is not documented here.
procedures.name: Factory reset from the SMART Assist app (server-signed)

steps.action: Start the brick on the SMART Charger, open SMART Assist signed in to the account that registered it, and choose the app's reset option.
The app reads 0x86, obtains a signature for a factory-reset command from LEGO's backend, writes it to 0x87, then writes register 0x95.
steps.expect: 03 87 01 after the signature write; the brick then resets.

ble.protocol: Cordio WDX device-configuration registers (01/02/03 framing) on 0xFEF6

methods.description: What node-smartplay does. With the brick started on the charger, scan, connect, open notifications in the vendor app's order, run the handshake reads, and keep the link alive with the keepalive write. Model, firmware, MAC, battery, name and volume then work with no signature and no pairing.
methods.name: Start the brick on its SMART Charger, then connect (no account)

steps.action: Set the brick on a SMART Charger so that it starts up there (pairing.enter_pairing_mode).
Close the SMART Assist app on any phone near by, so it is not holding the brick.
Scan for a connectable advertisement named exactly "Smart Brick" carrying company id 0x0397 and service 0xFEF6.
Connect, discover services, and run the top-level `initialization` sequence (notifications, handshake reads, keepalive, MTU read).
steps.expect: Notifications on 005f0002 of the form 03 RR ..., one per read. The brick may send an unprompted 03 02 ... frame before any command (protocol_details.wdx_registers.idle_beacon).

steps.action: Every ~500 ms, read 0x93 (charging/connection state), send the keepalive 02 90 ea 00, and read 0x20 (battery).
steps.expect: 03 93 xx and 03 20 xx replies; nothing comes back for the keepalive.

timing.notes: 500 ms is the vendor app's polling period as upstream captured it and node-smartplay copies it. The first CCCD write to the Control Point may fail; upstream retries after about 5 s. 10 s is node-smartplay's per-request timeout, not a device constant. Whether the brick drops the link when the keepalive stops is not established.

causes: The brick started up off the charger. It checks for the dock once, at boot; putting a running brick on the charger does not make it connectable. Let it restart on the charger.
The brick is in multi-brick play: it advertises "Smart Brick" as non-connectable alongside its PAwR train.
troubleshooting.symptom: A "Smart Brick" shows up in the scan but will not connect.

causes: It is asleep, or it started off the charger with single-brick content, which does not advertise.
It is in firmware-update mode, which uses a different advertisement (not documented).
troubleshooting.symptom: No "Smart Brick" in the scan at all.

causes: Upstream saw the first CCCD write to 005f0002 fail; wait about 5 s and write it again.
troubleshooting.symptom: Turning on notifications for the Control Point fails.

causes: Something read register 0x86 (the signed-command nonce). That read makes the brick ask for link-layer pairing; node-smartplay avoids it for this reason. Nothing on the unauthenticated surface needs it.
troubleshooting.symptom: The phone suddenly asks to pair.

causes: Register 0x85 was not 0: an update is in progress (1) or the battery is too low (2). The vendor app checks 0x85 before writing 0x81.
The value was not 10, 40 or 100, the three levels the app uses.
troubleshooting.symptom: A volume write does not take.

cloud.local_alternative: Yes for battery, name, volume and device info (the primary method). None known for registration, telemetry consent, factory reset or firmware updates: each needs a signature only LEGO's servers can make.

methods.description: The vendor route. The app talks to the same docked brick over the same registers, and adds what needs LEGO's backend: registering the brick to a LEGO account (ownership), telemetry consent, factory reset and firmware updates, each through a server-signed command. It is not needed for the local read/control surface above, and none of those operations can be done without LEGO's servers.
methods.name: LEGO SMART Assist app with a LEGO account (registration, updates)

steps.action: Install LEGO SMART Assist and sign in with a LEGO account.
Start the brick on the SMART Charger and follow the app's steps to add or update it.
For a privileged operation, the app reads the nonce (0x86), gets a signature from LEGO's backend, writes it to 0x87, then writes the operation's register.
steps.expect: 03 87 01 for an accepted signature, 03 87 00 for a rejected one.

setup.notes: Nothing is provisioned for local use: no Wi-Fi, no account, no bond. The one physical precondition is that the brick started up on its SMART Charger (see pairing.enter_pairing_mode). The LEGO account, registration and firmware updates exist only through the vendor app and LEGO's backend. Confidence medium: upstream captures of the vendor app plus a published open client, not replayed here.

rejoin.notes: There is no network to rejoin, and the local surface is bound to no phone: any client can read and set it once the brick has started on the charger. Moving the brick between LEGO accounts is a registration question for the vendor app and LEGO's backend (the ownership-proof register is signature-gated), not a BLE one.

testing.notes: No capture and no hardware session by this project. The facts rest on the node-smartplay research notes, whose authors report Android HCI captures of the vendor app, and on the node-smartplay library, which its author publishes as working for battery, volume, naming and device info. That supports per-fact `verification: reported`, not this flag.

entities.name: Battery
entities.notes: The brick answers only when asked: send read_battery_level (01 20) and decode the 03 20 xx reply. The vendor app polls every ~500 ms along with the keepalive.

entities.name: Volume
entities.notes: Read the current level with read_volume (reply 03 81 xx); the Control Point's `format` decodes battery frames only, so that reply is parsed by register (protocol_details.wdx_registers). Check read_upgrade_state is 0 before writing, as the vendor app does.

evidence.community_implementations: node-smartplay 1.0.0 (npm, declares MIT; the same code as the GitHub main branch): scan filter (0xFEF6 plus company 0x0397), CCCD order, handshake, keepalive, 500 ms polling, set-volume with the 0x85 check, set-name with a 12-byte limit and read-back, and the note that reading 0x86 triggers pairing. Its author lists battery, volume, naming and device info as supported and authentication as not.
evidence.documentation_review: LEGO's SMART Play getting-started page, SMART Assist app page and "How we made" article (Wayback copies, 2026): shake to wake, charger LED battery colours, wireless charging of up to two bricks, the sensor list, the app's role (battery, registration, updates) and the August 2026 firmware release. No user manual PDF for the brick or charger was found, and LEGO's help-centre articles are not archived.
evidence.fcc: Our manuals pass recorded grant NPI106929 ("Smart brick", LEGO System A/S, 2025-12-10) on fccid.co, with label, test-report, RF-exposure and antenna exhibits and no user manual. The grant page could not be re-fetched when this spec was written (fccid.co answered 404, fccid.io 403), so the ID is carried as unconfirmed.
evidence.identifiers_checked: Bluetooth SIG assigned numbers (fetched 2026-09-28): company 0x0397 = LEGO System A/S; member UUID 0xFEF6 = Wicentric, Inc. IEEE OUI 9C:9A:C0 = LEGO System A/S (this repository's registries/ieee-oui.tsv).
evidence.open_questions: Everything is unreplayed here. Open in upstream too: the 3ff2 service, the idle beacon (our Cordio reading is a hypothesis), 0x93's bits, the undocumented 0x83/0x92/0x94, the file-transfer format, the 0x02 layout, whether writes are answered, whether the keepalive is required, and the signed-command suffix.
evidence.open_source_stack: Packetcraft/Arm Cordio (packetcraft-inc/stacks master 3656312, Apache-2.0): wdx_defs.h (base UUID, characteristic roles, device-configuration ops and parameter ids 0x01-0x25, lengths), wdxs_dc.c (reply layouts, including the connection-parameter update) and wdxs_main.c (update sent on each connection-update event), svc_wdxs.c (characteristic properties). The match between those and upstream's register map is exact for 0x01-0x25; that is why the stock meanings are carried here.
evidence.public_research: node-smartplay research notes (nathankellenicki, main 5b46706, fetched 2026-09-28). PROTOCOL.md: advertisement, GATT layout, framing, register map, connection lifecycle, volume sequence, signed-command layout and what needs it; its authors say it comes from Android HCI captures and a decompile of the vendor app, may contain errors, and that some payloads are encrypted. FIRMWARE.md: reply sizes per register and the connectable-at-boot analysis (addresses deliberately not carried over). FILE_TRANSFER.md: the firmware-update outline, which it labels inferred. BACKEND.md: that the signing key is server-held and the app only relays the nonce. HARDWARE.md: the EM9305 SoC and the custom LEGO ASIC. The repository has no licence file; nothing is copied verbatim.

dfu_mode.notes: Upstream's firmware analysis names a distinct update-mode advertisement; its name and contents are not documented.

enter.notes: Upstream's outline (which it calls inferred from the decompiled app): check 0x85 == 0, upload the image through the WDX file-transfer characteristics (005f0003 / 005f0004) in chunks of at most 100 bytes, verify it, then write register 0x26, which disconnects, arms the update and resets the brick. Starting an upgrade needs a server-signed command (type 4), and 0x26 is signature-gated too. No entry or transfer bytes are declared here: a replacement client cannot sign, and a broken transfer is the one way to damage the brick over BLE.

image.notes: The app downloads firmware from LEGO's backend. Upstream's notes list a signature field in the update image header and find the signed-command public key inside the firmware image; the image signature algorithm itself is not established. The header also names a second product (upstream reads it as the charging panel).

dfu.notes: Recorded so a client knows updates exist, arrive only through the vendor app with LEGO's signature, and must not be interrupted. The LEGO SMART Assist page for the August 2026 Pokémon release says bricks from earlier sets needed an app update to play with the new sets.

initialization.notes: First in the vendor app's CCCD order. This channel then sends empty notifications now and then; their purpose is unknown.
The Control Point. Upstream saw the first CCCD write here fail at times; retry after about 5 s.
Service Changed, last in the vendor app's order. Opening the file-transfer and Service Changed channels is copied from the app; nothing here uses them.

Handshake read of the firmware revision: reply 03 22 + a 16-byte null-padded ASCII string. The vendor app runs this four-read handshake three times; node-smartplay runs it once and also reads the model (0x21) and battery (0x20).
Handshake read of the volume: reply 03 81 + 0x0a, 0x28 or 0x64.
Handshake read of the brick's MAC: reply 03 84 + six bytes, most-significant first. This is the stable identity.
Handshake read of the brick's name: reply 03 80 + up to 12 bytes of UTF-8, null-padded.
Keepalive. No reply. The app then repeats it in its ~500 ms polling loop.
ATT MTU read: reply 03 08 + uint16 little-endian (f4 00 = 244 in upstream's capture). The app does not read the nonce (0x86) unless it is about to sign; neither should a local client.

Advertisement.description: Manufacturer-specific AD data. On the air: 97 03 (company 0x0397, little-endian) then a payload. Upstream captured the whole structure as 97 03 00 60 00 00 00 00 from a docked brick.

fields.description: Bytes after the company id: 00 60 00 00 00 00 in the one capture published. Meaning unknown; do not match on it.
fields.name: payload

parse_rules: Require company id 0x0397 (919), the exact local name "Smart Brick" and a connectable advertising PDU.
AD flags 0x06 (LE General Discoverable, BR/EDR not supported).
The address is LE random and rotates; do not store it as identity.

ConnectionParameters.description: Hypothesis: the value of register 0x02 and of the unprompted "idle beacon", laid out as the open-source Cordio WDX profile sends its connection-parameter update (wdxs_dc.c). Upstream reports the register and the beacon bytes; the field meanings below are ours, from the stack source, and unconfirmed on a brick.
ConnectionParameters.example: 03 02 00 0c 00 00 00 f4 01  (status 0; interval 12 x 1.25 = 15 ms; latency 0; timeout 500 x 10 = 5000 ms)

fields.description: uint8, HCI status of the last connection update; 0 = success.
fields.name: status

RegisterReply.description: Every Control Point notification: 03, the register byte, then the value in the layout the register map gives.

fields.description: 0x03 = reply or unsolicited update (01 and 02 are the request types and never come back).
fields.name: frame_type

fields.description: The register the value belongs to.
fields.name: register

parse_rules: Match by register, not by order: the brick may send 03 02 ... before any request.
No status byte: a rejected write is noticed only by reading the register back.

SignedCommand.description: The 75-byte value written to register 0x87 (77 bytes on the Control Point with the 02 87 prefix).
SignedCommand.example: 02 87 01 23 45 67 89 ab cd ef 02 02 01 <32 bytes r> <32 bytes s>  (invented nonce; SHA-256 of 0123456789abcdef020201 = 5c8468499fbcba5e62727e9301ff46ec15ad99f4ba916376a81f1705b6592bf6)

fields.description: Bytes 0-7: the 8-byte nonce just read from register 0x86, unchanged.
fields.name: nonce_echo

parse_rules: Signed message: SHA-256 over nonce (8 bytes) || command_suffix (3 bytes), 11 bytes in all.
Signature: ECDSA P-256 over that digest with LEGO's server-held private key, r || s, 64 bytes.

lifecycle.cccd_note: The first CCCD write to 005f0002 may fail; retry after about 5 s.
connectable_rule: Booted on a charger (one of two dock types): connectable advertising.
Booted off the charger, single-brick content: no advertising.
Booted off the charger, multi-brick content: non-connectable "Smart Brick" advertising alongside PAwR on another address.
Lifted off after booting docked: probably stays connectable (upstream inference; advertising restarts after each disconnect without re-checking the dock).
Firmware update: its own update-mode advertising only.
lifecycle.description: The vendor app's connection as upstream captured it; node-smartplay follows it.
lifecycle.handshake_note: The app runs the four reads three times over. node-smartplay reads 0x21, 0x22, 0x81, 0x84, 0x80, 0x20 once.

signed_command.command_types_note: Upstream lists the four types but publishes only one suffix, 02 02 01, with its captures. Whether that suffix's last byte is the type (1 = unlock) is not established.
signed_command.description: Challenge-response for the privileged operations. The brick verifies an ECDSA P-256 signature against a public key built into its firmware; the matching private key exists only on LEGO's servers, which sign for the signed-in owner when the app asks. Upstream recovered the public key from captured signatures and found it in the firmware; it is not reproduced here because a client has no use for it. Upstream also checked that each captured signature used a fresh random value (all r values distinct), which rules out recovering the private key through reuse.
flow: 1. Read 0x86: reply 03 86 + an 8-byte nonce, fresh per connection. This read makes the brick request link-layer pairing.
3. digest = SHA-256(message); signature = ECDSA-P256-sign(LEGO private key, digest) as r || s, 32 bytes each, big-endian.
4. Write 02 87 + nonce + 02 02 01 + r + s (75 value bytes).
5. Reply 03 87 01 = verified, 03 87 00 = rejected. Then write the operation's register.

test_vector.note: Checks message construction only; no valid signature can be given without LEGO's key.

wdx_registers.description: The register protocol on the Control Point, restated in our own words from node-smartplay's PROTOCOL.md and FIRMWARE.md, with the standard meaning of 0x01-0x25 cross-checked against the open-source Cordio WDX profile (wdx_defs.h, wdxs_dc.c). Sizes are value bytes, without the 03 RR header. `auth` means the brick acts only after a server-signed command in the same connection.

framing.notes: One frame per ATT write, never split. Every request on the unauthenticated surface fits a default 23-byte MTU (the longest, a 12-byte name write, is 14 bytes). The 0x87 signed command is 77 bytes, so it needs an ATT MTU of at least 80; upstream's capture shows 244.
framing.reply: 03 RR VV... (notification on the same characteristic)
framing.stack_origin: Cordio WDX device-configuration operations get (0x01), set (0x02) and update (0x03).

idle_beacon.interpretation: It has the exact shape of the stock Cordio WDX connection-parameter update, which that stack sends on every link connection-update event (wdxs_main.c): register 0x02, status 0, interval 15 ms, latency 0, supervision timeout 5 s. If so it is not a beacon at all but the brick reporting the parameters the central just negotiated, and it may recur whenever they change. Unconfirmed on a brick.
idle_beacon.observed: Sent by the brick unprompted, before any request (upstream calls it an idle beacon; node-smartplay treats it as an unsolicited notification).

out_of_scope: 0x1B and 0x1C, and the PAwR reuse of 0x25 and 0x26: brick-to-brick play, handled by a separate internal path, not used by the app.
The file-transfer protocol on 005f0003 / 005f0004 (firmware, fault log, telemetry).

registers.notes: Cordio layout: min interval, max interval, latency, timeout, each uint16 LE (hypothesis). Not used by the app.

registers.role: Ask the brick to start link security

registers.notes: Whether LEGO implements it is not documented.
Upstream's firmware sizes show no value bytes; unclear.
Upstream also lists 0x25 among the PAwR play registers handled by a separate internal path; that use is out of scope.
The last step of a firmware update. Also reused internally for PAwR play (out of scope). No bytes documented here.
Part of the file-transfer machinery; layout not documented here.
Upstream's two tables disagree on its size (4 bytes vs a 4-byte reply including the header).

registers.role: Upgrade state: 0 ready, 1 in progress, 2 low battery

registers.notes: Reading it makes the brick request link-layer pairing.

registers.role: Firmware build fingerprint (same on every brick upstream checked)

registers.notes: Not tag data: it is one byte.

registers.role: Unknown; upstream reads it as a hardware timer

registers.notes: Upstream's firmware table shows an empty write; the effect and read layout are not documented. Not declared as a command.

remaining_unknowns: Nothing has been run against a brick by this project. First check: connect to a brick started on the charger, run the handshake, read 0x20 and 0x84.
What the 3ff2 service is for: 005f0009 (write-only) and the empty periodic notifications on 005f000a.
Whether the unprompted 03 02 ... frame is the Cordio connection-parameter update this spec guesses (and so recurs on every parameter change), and the true layout of register 0x02.
What the bits of 0x93 mean (only 0xa1 reported).
What the undocumented registers 0x83, 0x92 and 0x94 hold; whether 0x92 changes when a SMART Tag is placed.
Which writes the brick answers: the volume write (node-smartplay waits for 03 81; upstream shows no reply), the name write, and writes to unknown registers.
Whether the brick drops the link, or stops being connectable, when the keepalive stops.
Whether volume values other than 10, 40 and 100 are accepted, and what a short name write leaves in the name field.
Whether the 0x87 suffix 02 02 01 encodes the signed-command type, and how types 2-4 are sent.
The link-layer association model when reading 0x86 triggers pairing, whether a bond is kept, and whether 0x07 (delete bonds) works.
How many centrals the brick accepts at once.
What a factory reset clears, and what travel mode (0x96) does and how it is left.
The model string in 0x21, and the number-to-stage mapping of 0x89.
The WDX file-transfer format, the firmware image signature algorithm, the update-mode advertisement, and what an interrupted update does. Deliberately not probed.

characteristics.name: Device Name
characteristics.notes: "Smart Brick" per upstream. Whether it follows the name set in register 0x80 is not documented.

services.name: Generic Attribute
services.notes: Present by implication: upstream's CCCD order ends with Service Changed. Properties are the Bluetooth core default, not observed.

characteristics.name: Firmware Revision String
characteristics.notes: Version string, e.g. "2.29.2" in upstream's capture.

characteristics.name: Software Revision String
characteristics.notes: Same string as the firmware revision in upstream's capture.

services.name: Device Information
services.notes: Standard Device Information strings. The same firmware version is also in register 0x22.

keepalive.description: Write register 0x90 with ea 00. No reply. The vendor app sends it once after the handshake and then in every ~500 ms poll.

read_att_mtu.description: Read register 0x08, the link's ATT MTU. Reply 03 08 + uint16 little-endian (f4 00 = 244 in upstream's capture; varies with the central).

read_battery_level.description: Read register 0x20, battery level. Reply 03 20 + uint8 percent (0-100).

read_build_stage.description: Read register 0x89. Reply 03 89 + uint8, the build pipeline stage (development, QA, staging or release). The number-to-stage mapping is not documented.

read_charging_state.description: Read register 0x93, charging/connection state. Reply 03 93 + uint8. Only 0xa1 has been reported (a docked, connected brick); the meaning of the bits is unknown.

read_connection_parameters.description: Read register 0x02, the current connection parameters. The register is reported upstream; the reply layout is a hypothesis from the Cordio WDX source: 03 02, status (uint8), connection interval (uint16 LE, x1.25 ms), peripheral latency (uint16 LE, events), supervision timeout (uint16 LE, x10 ms). See payload_formats.ConnectionParameters.

read_firmware_revision.description: Read register 0x22, firmware version. Reply 03 22 + 16 bytes, ASCII, null-padded (e.g. "2.29.2").

read_mac_address.description: Read register 0x84, the brick's MAC. Reply 03 84 + six bytes, most-significant octet first (upstream's example starts 9c 9a c0, LEGO's OUI). The stable identity; the advertised address is random.

read_model.description: Read register 0x21, the model identifier. Reply 03 21 + a null-terminated string in an 18-byte field (upstream's firmware reply sizes; the Cordio stack's standard model length). Its content is not quoted upstream.

read_name.description: Read register 0x80, the brick's name. Reply 03 80 + up to 12 bytes UTF-8, null-terminated or null-padded; stop at the first 0x00. Default "Smart Brick".

read_update_fingerprint.description: Read register 0x88. Reply 03 88 + 20 bytes that upstream reads as a SHA-1-sized fingerprint and reports identical across bricks, so it describes the firmware build rather than the unit. Upstream's backend notes use a value of the same role to select a firmware download.

read_upgrade_state.description: Read register 0x85. Reply 03 85 + uint8: 0 ready, 1 update in progress, 2 battery too low. The app requires 0 before writing volume.

read_volume.description: Read register 0x81, volume. Reply 03 81 + uint8: 10 (0x0a) low, 40 (0x28) medium, 100 (0x64) high.

set_name.description: Write register 0x80: the new name as raw UTF-8, at most 12 bytes, no terminator (what node-smartplay sends). Do not wait for a reply; read 0x80 back to confirm. Whether a shorter name leaves stale bytes behind is not documented; the read-back shows it.

name.description: UTF-8; the limit is 12 BYTES, not characters, so multi-byte characters count more than once.

set_volume.description: Write register 0x81. The vendor app first reads 0x85 and writes only when it is 0 (ready), then reads 0x81 back to confirm. Only the three levels below are known; other values are untested.

level.description: Volume level code. The numbers look like percentages but only these three are used.

format_match.notes: Only 03 20 frames (battery level) are decoded by `format`.

characteristics.name: Control Point (WDX device configuration)
characteristics.notes: Every register read and write goes here as an ATT Write Request (node-smartplay writes with response). Frames: read 01 RR, write 02 RR VV..., reply 03 RR VV... by notification, where RR is the register byte and VV its value. A reply echoes the register it answers, so match replies to requests by register and keep one request per register outstanding. There is no status or error code in a reply. Replies to writes are not reliable to wait for: the keepalive gets none, node-smartplay does not wait after a name write, and does wait for a 03 81 reply after a volume write; upstream shows none for that write. Confirm a write with a read. The full register map is protocol_details.wdx_registers. The `format` below decodes battery replies only (03 20 xx); other replies are laid out in the register map.

characteristics.name: WDX file transfer control
characteristics.notes: Upstream calls it data channel 1 and saw it carry file-transfer requests and acknowledgements (on-device files: firmware, fault log, telemetry). Cordio's name for it is File Transfer Control. Upstream calls its own description of the transfer format inferred. Not documented here; do not write to it.

characteristics.name: WDX file transfer data
characteristics.notes: Upstream's data channel 2: the file payload stream. Cordio's File Transfer Data. Not documented here.

characteristics.name: WDX authentication
characteristics.notes: Upstream's data channel 3, idle in normal use. Cordio's Authentication characteristic (its own challenge scheme); LEGO's signed commands go through register 0x87 on the Control Point instead. Whether anything uses this one is unknown.

services.name: WDX (Cordio Wireless Data Exchange)
services.notes: The Cordio stack's WDX service; its four characteristics share the base 005fxxxx-2ff2-4ed5-b045-4c7463617865 (the trailing bytes spell "exactLE" backwards, the stack's original name). The UUIDs and properties below match the open-source Cordio definitions exactly, where 0002 is Device Configuration, 0003 File Transfer Control, 0004 File Transfer Data and 0005 Authentication. Upstream observed 0003 and 0004 carrying file transfers and 0005 idle in normal use. Only 0002 is needed for this spec's surface.

characteristics.name: Unknown write-only input
characteristics.notes: Accepts writes without visible effect or reply (upstream). Purpose unknown; nothing here writes to it.

characteristics.name: Unknown bidirectional channel
characteristics.notes: Sends empty notifications periodically once subscribed (upstream). Purpose unknown.

services.name: LEGO custom service (3ff2 base)
services.notes: A second service on the base 005fxxxx-3ff2-4ed5-b045-4c7463617865 (service UUID as node-smartplay declares it). Purpose unknown; the vendor app subscribes to 000a first of all.
